title: How King's Edge creates lasting graduate value

strategicChallenge.title: The strategic challenge
paragraphs: The traditional graduate premium is becoming less secure. Graduate employment is under pressure, artificial intelligence is reshaping early-career work, and students are asking more exacting questions about the value and return on investment of higher education.

These pressures are unfolding in an increasingly competitive market. King’s faces more ambitious global competitors, while a shrinking domestic demographic will make competition for UK students more intense over time. Universities will need to make a clearer and more distinctive case for why students should choose them, and for the lasting value their education will provide.

King’s approaches this challenge from a position of considerable strength. It performs relatively well on employability, has a powerful global reputation and gives students access to an exceptional range of academic, professional, civic, cultural and international opportunities.

Yet the full value of that offer is not experienced consistently or expressed coherently. Opportunities remain unevenly available and are often organised through complex, noisy and disconnected structures. Students are left to work out what is available, what is relevant to them and how different experiences contribute to their development. Much of the employability value created through a King’s education therefore remains implicit and under-articulated, both to students and to the wider world.

The sector is already responding by placing greater emphasis on skills, employability and graduate outcomes. That direction of travel is quickly becoming a baseline expectation. The strategic question for King’s is how far it is willing to go: whether it follows the sector through incremental improvement, or uses its existing strengths to establish a more ambitious, distinctive and future-focused account of how a university education creates lasting graduate value.

strategicProposition.title: The strategic proposition
paragraphs: King’s will establish a more ambitious model of university education, organised around the graduate futures of its students.

Disciplinary study will remain the academic core of a King’s education. Around that core, every student will be actively supported to develop a clearer sense of purpose, explore their ambitions and build the learning, experiences, relationships and capabilities they need to take meaningful steps towards them.

This requires King’s to organise itself differently. The university will connect curriculum, opportunity, community, support and graduate futures more intentionally around the student, rather than expecting students to navigate a complex institution and assemble a coherent journey for themselves.

The relationship is reciprocal. Students will bring their interests, questions, experiences and evolving ambitions. King’s will respond by making relevant opportunities easier to access, strengthening the experiences available and helping students connect what they study with what they want to learn, do and contribute.

Graduate futures will therefore become a defining purpose of the whole King’s experience, rather than a separate outcome addressed primarily through careers provision or at the point of transition into work.

The ambition is that every student leaves King’s having been supported to move closer to a future that matters to them, with the knowledge, experience, connections and confidence to take their next step. King’s, in turn, will be able to offer a clearer, more distinctive and more credible account of the lasting value of a King’s education.

innovationAnchors.title: Our innovation anchors
innovationAnchors.introduction: Across the sector, universities are making increasingly prominent commitments around employability, skills and graduate outcomes. King’s Edge goes further. It builds on the distinctive intellectual value of disciplinary education by creating a second, connected dimension of educational gain around purpose, experience and future contribution.

items.title: Purpose as architecture
paragraphs: Most universities organise the student journey primarily around the course. Individual purpose, ambition and future direction are then addressed around it through careers support, optional opportunities and student initiative.

King’s will treat purpose as an organising principle alongside the disciplinary journey. Every student will be actively supported to explore what matters to them and to accrue the learning, experiences and connections needed to move towards it.

The two dimensions strengthen one another. Disciplinary study expands what students know, understand and can imagine. Purpose helps them connect that learning with the questions they want to pursue and the contribution they may want to make.

items.title: Learning design over activity guarantees
paragraphs: Across the sector, universities are making easily communicated promises about placements, projects and quantities of employer-informed learning.

King’s will lead through the quality and sophistication of its learning design. Students will encounter experiences that allow them to apply, test and extend their disciplinary learning through meaningful challenge, agency, relationships, reflection and work in unfamiliar settings.
Our ambition is to lead the sector in designing education intentionally around graduate futures, rather than relying on participation in a named activity as a proxy for development.

items.title: A developmental ecology engineered around every student
paragraphs: Universities often offer extensive opportunities around the course, but leave students to find, navigate and combine them for themselves.

King’s will build an intentional ecology of curricular, co-curricular and extra-curricular learning, world-leading in its quality, extent and inclusivity. It will increase the availability of innovative developmental experiences while making access to them more consistent.

The course provides the intellectual and disciplinary foundation. Around and through it, every student will be able to apply knowledge, build capabilities, form relationships, enter new communities and take meaningful steps towards their purposes.

items.title: An external skills language grounded in individual evidence
paragraphs: Graduate attributes frameworks usually describe a small set of qualities the university wants associated with its graduates. They are often too reductive to capture the breadth and specificity of what students develop, particularly as the capabilities needed in a changing world continue to evolve.

They also tend to map what a course is intended to provide, rather than what an individual student has actually developed through their particular combination of study, experience and participation. This weakens both relevance and assurance.
Most fundamentally, graduate attributes are usually an internal language: an account of how a university wants to describe its educational product.

King’s will instead use a rich, external skills language designed to broker a connection between disciplinary learning, individual experience and the wider world. It will allow students to build a more precise account of their own development, enable King’s to evidence that development more credibly, and connect the education more directly with changing forms of work and contribution.

causalHypothesis.title: Our causal hypothesis
paragraphs: If King’s treats disciplinary learning and individual purpose as connected organising principles, designs experiences around the development they produce, creates a rich and inclusive ecology of opportunity, and gives students an external language through which to recognise and evidence their capabilities, then every student will be better able to accrue and use the learning, experience and connections needed to move towards their ambitions.

Because King’s will understand those individual journeys more clearly, it will also be able to identify where graduate value is strong or uneven, respond more intelligently to student needs, strengthen its educational offer and make a more credible claim about the lasting value of a King’s education.
The result is a reciprocal learning system: King’s shapes itself around enabling student futures, and insight from those journeys continuously improves the education it provides.

items.title: more and better opportunities within and beyond the course
paragraphs: King’s will connect and strengthen what already exists, while substantially increasing the range of experiences through which students can apply their learning, develop skills, build relationships and explore their futures.
Every student will be supported to find and take part in opportunities relevant to their ambitions, circumstances and stage of development.

items.title: every student’s education is shaped by purpose as well as discipline
paragraphs: Alongside their disciplinary journey, every student will be supported to explore what matters to them and how their ambitions are developing.
King’s will use that understanding to connect students with relevant learning, experiences, relationships and support, helping them take meaningful steps towards futures that matter to them.

items.title: every student can recognise and explain what they have gained
paragraphs: A skills language understood beyond King’s, together with a richer record of learning, will help students talk confidently about the knowledge and capabilities they have developed through their course and wider experience.

Learning gained beyond the course will become more visible and, where appropriate, formally recognised. King’s will empower students to claim their individual learning gains rather than presuming that everyone develops in the same way.

items.title: King’s uses evidence to understand students and keep improving
paragraphs: King’s will connect what students tell us about their ambitions, needs and confidence; what they choose to take part in; what enrolment, course and graduate outcomes data reveals; and what employers, alumni, professions and wider society tell us about changing futures.

This will show where graduate value is strong, uneven or needs to change. King’s will use that insight to improve its courses, opportunities and support, and respond more closely to what students need.

items.title: stronger graduate futures strengthen King’s
paragraphs: Students are better equipped to move into positive graduate destinations and make confident next steps.

As those gains become visible in outcomes, evidence and external recognition, King’s will be able to make a stronger claim for the value of its education. This will sharpen its market position, support recruitment and conversion, strengthen relationships with employers and partners, and build its reputation as a leader in graduate futures.
